info.title: Naoero Airlines API
info.description:
The Naoero API sits between the Naoero Airlines clients (the mobile app now, the website next) and the airline's
**Zenith Sales API**. It holds the Zenith key, validates every request, keeps customer records in PostgreSQL and logs
every call. Clients never call Zenith directly.

**Base URL:** `https://api.napacificbridge.info` (app API under `/api/v1`, website content API under `/api`). The earlier address `https://naoero.37.60.224.111.nip.io` serves the same backend for older app builds.

## Conventions
- JSON in and out (`Content-Type: application/json`), except the profile photo (raw image bytes).
- Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`; timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC. Flight times are **local airport times** without a zone.
- Every error has the same shape: `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } }`. `message` is always safe to
  show to a customer; branch on `code`. Booking validation errors also carry `problems` (field-level).
- Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header; quote it when reporting a problem (it finds the request in the
  server logs).
- Rate-limited responses (429) carry `Retry-After` (seconds).

## Authentication (shared by the app and the website)
1. **Sign up** (`POST /api/v1/auth/signup`) or **log in** (`POST /api/v1/auth/login`). Both return an access token and a
   refresh token.
2. Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` on protected endpoints. It lasts **15 minutes**.
3. Before it expires (or on a 401 `unauthenticated`), call `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` with the refresh token. You get
   a **new pair**; the old refresh token stops working immediately (rotation). Presenting an already-used refresh token
   ends that whole session (theft protection), answering 401 `session_expired`.
4. A session lasts 7 days after its last refresh, and 30 days at most; then the user logs in again.
5. `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` ends this session, the other sessions, or all of them.

**Website note:** keep the refresh token server-side or in an `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite` cookie set by the
website's own backend, never in `localStorage`. Accounts are shared: a customer created on the website can log in to
the app and vice versa (one Zenith customer, one Naoero record).

**Passwords** are checked by Zenith only and are never stored by this API in any form. Zenith compares passwords
without regard to letter case. Login only reaches Zenith for emails already registered here.

## Bookings and payment
`POST /api/v1/bookings/prepare` (confirm fare, get the passenger form) → `POST /api/v1/bookings` (create, seats held until
`timeLimit`) → `POST /api/v1/bookings/{pnr}/payments` (open the airline's payment page) → the page redirects to one of
the return addresses → `POST /api/v1/bookings/{pnr}/payments/{paymentId}` (the API asks Zenith whether tickets were issued).
The client's report of the payment result is never trusted as proof of payment.


## After booking (1.11.0)
Every amount comes from the airline (Zenith); clients only show it and collect payment. Never calculate a price in the client.

**Change flights** `GET /api/v1/bookings/{pnr}/change` (what can change) → `POST …/change/search` (new date) →
`POST …/change/quote` (the airline's price: its own lines such as `Penalty`, plus the fare difference, never negative) →
`POST …/change` (holds the new flights; the old ones stay) → `POST /api/v1/bookings/{pnr}/payments` with the amount in
`booking.pendingChange.amountDue`. **Always call payments, even when it is 0**: the change is only confirmed when the
airline issues the new tickets; otherwise it lapses at `pendingChange.timeLimit`. `DELETE …/change` keeps the original
flights. A cheaper new flight is not refunded (the original price is kept). Paid extras follow the airline's rules:
exchangeable ones move to the new flights, refundable ones reduce the amount, others are lost; the quote and the amount
due already include this.

**Add a trip** `POST …/add-trip/search` → `POST …/add-trip/quote` → `POST …/add-trip` → pay the booking's `amountDue`.

**Extras after booking** (bags, seats): `GET/POST …/extras`, then pay `amountDue` when it is above 0. A cheaper seat or a
removed paid extra is not refunded.

**Passenger details** `GET/POST …/passengers`: contact details and travel documents; names cannot change online.

**Split** `POST …/split`: passengers move to a booking of their own (returned as `newBooking`, also listed in My Trips).

**Check-in** `GET …/check-in` → `POST …/check-in` with a group; boarding passes are links in `boardingPasses`.
When the airline does not allow web check-in (fare or route), each passenger carries the airline's reasons.

**Flight status** `GET …/flight-status`: from the airline's departure boards, from the day before each flight.

**Refunds**: tickets are non-refundable; use `POST …/refund-requests` (reviewed by staff). Cancelling with a credit
(MCO) is not available online.


## Phone numbers (1.14.0)
Every phone number is validated for its country (Google libphonenumber) and stored and returned in **E.164**
(`+919899765000`), the format Zenith and SMS gateways use. Send the number as typed or in E.164; with it, send the
country picked in the phone picker (`phoneCountry`, ISO code) so numbers typed without their code, and shared codes
(+1 United States / Canada, +44...), are read correctly. Mobile numbers (sign-up, profile, a passenger's mobile phone)
must be able to receive text messages: landlines are refused. Build the picker from `GET /api/v1/reference/phone-codes`
(every country with its flag and dialling code).

## Ways to pay (1.15.0)
Ask `GET /api/v1/bookings/{pnr}/payment-options` for what the airline offers now in the booking's currency, show them, and send the chosen `code` as `fop` to `POST /api/v1/bookings/{pnr}/payments`. The list comes from the airline's configuration, so an option it adds appears without a new app release. Without `fop`, the airline's first option is used.

## Flight notices (1.16.0)
When the airline changes a flight's time, cancels a flight or moves passengers to another flight (and ticks "notify passengers"), Zenith posts the event to us, we reload the booking and add a notice for the customer who holds it. The app and the website show the same notices: poll `GET /api/v1/me/notifications/unread-count` for a badge (e.g. every minute while open, and on resume), open `GET /api/v1/me/notifications` to list them, and mark them read. Each notice has a `type` (`flight_time_change`, `flight_cancelled`, `flight_transfer`), a ready-to-show `title` and `body`, the booking's `pnr`, and `changes` with the flights before and after. The booking itself is already updated when the notice appears.

## Self-service (1.17.0)
What customers can do on their own with the airline's key:
- **Cancel** (`GET/POST /bookings/{pnr}/cancel`, Zenith PrepareCancel / Cancel). An unpaid booking is released whole (`mode: booking`) or flight by flight (`mode: flights`); nothing is charged or refunded. A paid booking is cancelled with a refund (`mode: refund`) when the fare rules allow it: the amount goes to a **credit voucher** on the customer's account, never back to the card. Send the `refundAmount` you showed as `expectedRefund`; if the airline now quotes another amount nothing is done and `409 refund_changed` returns the new quote. Every attempt is recorded.
- **Vouchers** (`GET /me/vouchers`, LoadMCOTickets): credit left by refunds and changes, with amount, status and expiry.
- **Services sold on their own** (`GET /services`, `POST /services/purchase`, SearchServices / BuyServices): buying makes a booking of `kind: services`, paid with `POST /bookings/{pnr}/payments` like any booking.
- **Undo check-in** (`POST /bookings/{pnr}/check-in/undo`, Uncheck): off unless the airline enables it (`check-in` answers `undo.available`). It cancels the flights for those passengers as a no-show, so `confirm: true` is required.
- **Flown flights** (`GET /bookings/{pnr}/flown`, FlownCoupons): which coupons of the booking were flown.
- **Seat calendar** (`GET /flight-calendar`, Calendar): per day of a month, `available` (HK), `waitlist` (HL) or `full`. Seats, not fares.
- **Value codes** (`GET /reference/value-code-lists`, `GET /reference/value-codes/{name}`), and **health** now pings Zenith (`zenith.reachable`).

## Flights and tickets (1.17.1)
In Zenith a booking's flights (seats in the inventory) and its tickets have separate lifecycles. Cancelling the flights of a paid booking releases the seats but **keeps the tickets open**, still worth their fare: they can be changed to another flight or refunded later. Such a booking has `status: cancelled` with `keptTickets` set (`amount`, `canChange`, `canRefund`): show "Your flights are cancelled. Your tickets (amount) are still valid" with Change flight and, when offered, Refund.
For a paid booking `GET /bookings/{pnr}/cancel` can offer two ways: `refund` (to a credit voucher, only when the airline lets the key refund to MCO) and `keep_ticket` ("cancel flights only, keep the ticket value", only when the airline enables it). `ticketValue` is what the open tickets are worth.

## Shop inventory (1.18.0)
Merchandise is stocked per **variant**: a size, a colour, or the product itself when it has no options. Every product has `options` (e.g. `[{"name": "Size", "values": ["S", "M", "L"]}]`) and `variants`, each with its own `id`, `sku`, `price`, `inStock`, `stockLeft` and `maxQuantity`.
- When `hasVariants` is true, the customer picks a variant and the order line sends its `variantId`; without one the order is refused with 400 `variant_required`. A product without options has one variant: `variantId` can be left out.
- Before checkout, `POST /shop/cart/check` returns today's price and how many can be bought of each line (`problem`: `out_of_stock`, `not_enough_stock`, `variant_required`, `product_unavailable`). Nothing is reserved until the order is placed.
- Sold out? `POST /shop/stock-alerts` (signed in) asks to be told when it is back: the customer gets a `back_in_stock` notification (see Notifications) once, as soon as stock arrives.
- Stock is managed by staff in the admin panel (Shop & Gift Cards → Inventory): adjustments, purchase orders received from suppliers, stock counts, and refunds putting items back in stock. Orders hold stock while awaiting payment, sell it when paid and release it when not paid in time.

## Inbox and after the order (1.19.0)
**Notifications** now cover the whole project, each with a `category` (`flights`, `bookings`, `shop`, `account`) and an `action` saying what to open:
- Flights (from the airline): time changes, cancellations, transfers.
- Bookings: reserved, payment failed, confirmed (tickets issued), expired, flight change held / cancelled / confirmed, trip added, extras updated, passenger details updated, checked in, check-in undone, refund request received, cancelled / refunded / flights cancelled.
- Shop: order placed, paid, payment under review, cancelled, expired, refunded, gift card ready, every delivery step (packed, shipped, in transit, out for delivery, delivered, failed attempt), every return step, help replies, review replies, back in stock.
Each step notifies once. List with `?category=`, page with `?before=` (`nextBefore`), badge from `unreadByCategory`.

**Shop orders** (`GET /shop/orders/{id}`) now carry `delivery` (steps and every tracking update), `documents` (invoice and receipt links, valid 1 hour), `cancellation` (unpaid: cancelled; paid and not shipped, no gift card used: full refund to the card), `returnPolicy` and per-line `lines` (how many can be returned, review state), `returns`, `supportRequests` and `help`.
- Returns and exchanges: `POST /shop/orders/{id}/returns` within the return window after delivery; staff approve (with instructions), receive (restocking), then refund or send the replacement.
- Help: `POST /me/support-requests` (optionally about an order), a conversation with the shop team.
- Reviews: buyers only (paid, merchandise shipped), once per product; `GET /shop/products/{id}/reviews` for the rating summary and reviews.

## Push notifications (1.20.0)
Every new notice in the inbox is also pushed to the customer's phones: iPhones through Apple (APNs), Android through Firebase Cloud Messaging (only the delivery pipe). Device UIDs, push tokens and keys are kept in our database, not in the Zenith booking.
- `GET /push/config`: whether pushes are on for iOS and Android, and the Firebase app settings an Android phone needs to get a token.
- `PUT /me/devices/{uid}`: the app registers its install on every launch and sign-in, and whenever it gets a new token; also sets `pushEnabled` and `mutedCategories`.
- `GET /me/devices`, `DELETE /me/devices/{uid}` (on sign-out).
A phone gets pushes only while its sign-in session is active. Each push carries `notificationId`, `type`, `category`, `pnr`, `orderId` and `action` (JSON, as in the inbox), so tapping it opens the same screen.

## Account deletion (1.21.0)
`GET|POST|DELETE /me/delete-request`: the customer asks with a reason (`accountDeletionReasons`) and their password, and can withdraw. Nothing is deleted: staff disable the account in the admin panel (it can't sign in until re-enabled) or decline with a note the customer sees. `account_disabled` (403) is what a disabled account gets when signing in or using a session.

## Usernames (1.22.0)
Customers choose a username (Zenith's Login: unique, fixed); several accounts can share an email. Sign-up takes `username`, `birthDate`, `acceptTerms` and `marketingOptIn`; `GET /auth/username-available` checks a username as it is typed; sign-in takes `username` or `email` (`several_accounts` when the email has more than one account); the password reset takes `email` and/or `username`. Profiles have `username` and `email`. Older apps without a username keep working.

## Flight reminders (1.26.0)
Some hours before a flight Zenith posts a `FlightReminder` event (address `flight-reminder`); every customer holding the booking gets a `flight_reminder` notice (category `flights`, action `booking`) and a push: "Your flight is coming up", naming the flight and its local departure time. `changes` is empty; nothing about the booking changed. No reminder is sent for a flight the booking no longer holds.

post.description: Zenith LoadCustomer (ByLoginAndPassword) checks the password. An email not registered here is checked with Zenith too: an account created on the airline's booking site is added here on its first login (customer accounts only). If Zenith refuses it, the answer is 404 `email_not_registered` (Zenith can't tell an unknown email from a wrong password), and such an email gets 3 tries per 15 minutes. Limits: 5 failures per email and 30 per IP per 15 minutes (Zenith itself locks an account after about 4 failures). When a password reset was requested in the last 24 hours and other devices are signed in, `suggestSignOutOtherDevices` is true.

post.description: Zenith PrepareFlights confirms availability and the final price and lists the passenger data the airline requires for this route and these passengers. Returns the passenger form (build the UI from `form`, never hardcode fields), the confirmed price, values to pre-fill from the profile, and saved travellers with the passenger slots each can fill. The draft is valid 25 minutes. Limits: 30 per account per 15 minutes. The response includes `extras`: special services (meals, assistance, baggage & equipment, animals, seat preferences, lounge, a note), seat maps, paid extras such as extra baggage, mandatory fees and fare rules.

post.description:
Reloads the live amount due, then Zenith CreateTicket with the airline's online payment method (NAB). Open `redirectUrl` (navigate) or `html` (render) in a browser view / web page. Card details are entered on the airline's page only. Limits: 10 per account per hour.

**App:** no body. The page ends by navigating to `returnUrlPrefix` + `accept`, `decline` or `cancel` (an address that never loads); intercept it and call the result endpoint.

**Website:** send `returnUrl`. The page then returns to `GET /api/v1/bookings/payments/{paymentId}/return/{outcome}`, which sends the browser on to `returnUrl` with the booking reference, payment id and outcome; the website then calls the result endpoint for the real status.

Also confirms a held flight change, an added trip or extras added after booking: the amount is always the airline's `amountDue`. When it is 0 no payment page opens: the tickets are issued at once and `booking` is returned.

**The card form is always a page to open (1.13.0).** When the airline's online payment is a card form, `redirectUrl` is our own HTTPS page `https://api.napacificbridge.info/api/v1/bookings/payments/{paymentId}/form?t=…` and `html` is null, so the app's WebView and the browser show our address instead of `about:blank`. Open it as a normal page (navigate, or load it in a WebView); the card details still go straight to the airline. The link opens only while the payment is running and for 60 minutes; it closes once the result is reported.

post.summary: Receive a flight event from Zenith
post.description: Called by Zenith (EventMap), not by clients. The webhook key (`ZENITH_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, 64 random characters) is part of the address and tells us the call is Zenith's. Nothing is turned away: every post is saved and answered `200 OK`, so Zenith never has to retry a post we have. A post with a wrong or missing key (or from an IP not on the allowlist) is saved as unverified and notifies no customer unless staff process it; a post to an event we don't know is saved and not acted on. Subscribed events: `flight-change` (FlightChange), `segment-flight-cancelled` (SegmentFlightCancelled), `flight-transfer` (FlightTransfer), `flight-reminder` (FlightReminder, some hours before each flight). In preproduction Zenith adds `test` to the event, in lowercase (e.g. `flight-changetest`); the address is read ignoring case. The body is JSON (inside an `EventMapNotification`) or XML as Zenith sends it (an `<Event>` with the flight's details followed by a `<Data>` with the customer and a `LoadBookingRequest`, declared `utf-16`; UTF-16 or UTF-8 bytes are both read), or JSON. A post, or a repeat of one, is answered `200 OK` once stored and processed in the background. Every call, accepted or refused, is saved with the response we sent (the key is never saved or logged).

itemsSummary.description: What was bought, for list rows

delivery.description: One order only (not in the history list).

lines.description: Per order line, in the order of `items`.

filters.description: The filters applied, as understood by the server

summary.description: Totals over all of the customer’s orders (filters do not apply)

stockLeft.description: Only set when 10 or fewer are left across all variants.

hasVariants.description: The customer must pick one of `variants` (send its `variantId`).

variants.description: Active variants, in order; empty for gift cards.

ShopVariant.description: One stocked version of a product: a size, a colour, or the product itself.

title.description: null for a product without options.

stockLeft.description: Only set when 10 or fewer are left (0 when sold out).

maxQuantity.description: The most one order can take of it now: the per-order limit or what is left.

email.description: The customer's email; stored lower-case. Several accounts may use the same email. Without username it is also the login.

phone.description: Mobile number (must receive text messages). As typed or E.164; stored and returned in E.164. Validated for its country.

deviceLabel.description: Shown in session lists, e.g. "Website" or "android app".

phoneCountry.description: Country picked in the phone picker (ISO code).

username.description: The login the customer signs in with: unique across all accounts and fixed once created. 3-50 characters: letters, numbers, dots, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter or number; no repeated or trailing dots/underscores/hyphens; some names are reserved. Check it first with GET /api/v1/auth/username-available.

birthDate.description: Required with username. Not in the future.

acceptTerms.description: Required (true) with username: the conditions of carriage, fare rules, baggage policy, privacy policy and the dangerous goods restrictions. The time is kept.

marketingOptIn.description: Consent to marketing emails and texts (offers, upgrades, surveys). Optional; the time is kept.

SignupRequest.description: A new account, as on the airline's "Create a new profile" form: login (username) and password, title, names, email, birth date, a mobile, and the GDPR choices. Without username (older apps) the email is the login, and birthDate and acceptTerms are optional.

variantId.description: null: any of the product's options.

status.description: open: waiting for the shop team; answered: waiting for the customer.

currentFare.description: Flight changes only: what the current tickets cost.

problems.message: The document must still be valid after your last flight.
Each infant must travel on the lap of a different adult.

status.description: Zenith's MCOStatusCode; `Issued` is the usable one.
